text.text:
Four protocols across nine years. One consistent design philosophy: borrow trust from systems people already believe in.

In 2016, I published DN-Key: broadcasting cryptographic public keys as DNS TXT records. Verification is a lookup. That's it. Adopted by regulated custody providers because compliance teams could understand it in one meeting. Cited by name in the Securities Commission Malaysia's capital markets blueprint.

Nine years later, the same protocol powers passkey-native, chain-agnostic identity across Bitcoin, EVM, and Solana. No modifications. No upgrades. It was forward-compatible with systems that didn't exist when it was written.

The gap between "too simple to be interesting" and "simple enough to survive nine years of platform evolution" is where protocol design actually lives.
